learn.hook: The beach is full of shells! How can we count them fast?
points: Put things in groups of the same size.
Count group by group to find how many in all.
Groups of 2, 5 or 10 are easy to count.
Grouping does not change the total. It only makes counting easy.

example.q: Aisha has 3 groups of 5 shells. How many shells?

learn.reallife: Mummy counts socks in pairs. The fruit seller counts bananas in bunches.

games.title: True or false?
items: Putting things in groups changes how many there are.
The total stays the same. Groups only make counting easy.

quiz.q: Riya puts shells in 4 groups of 5. How many shells?
quiz.explain: Count by 5s for 4 groups: 5, 10, 15, 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 5 instead of counting 4 groups of 5

quiz.q: Arjun makes 3 groups of 10 pebbles. How many pebbles?
quiz.explain: Count by 10s for 3 groups: 10, 20, 30.
quiz.mistake: Writes 1 and 3 together or adds 3 and 10

quiz.q: There are 6 pairs of slippers on the sand. How many slippers?
quiz.explain: A pair is 2. Count by 2s six times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.
quiz.mistake: Counts pairs instead of slippers

quiz.q: Meena counts starfish: 10, 20, 30, 40. How many groups of 10 is that?
quiz.explain: She said 4 numbers: 10, 20, 30, 40. So there are 4 groups of 10.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total instead of the number of groups

quiz.q: Why do we count shells in groups?
quiz.explain: Groups help us count fast with fewer mistakes. The number of shells stays the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks grouping changes the total

quiz.q: Kabir sees 2 groups of 5 crabs and 3 more crabs. How many crabs?
quiz.explain: 2 groups of 5 is 10. Then 3 more: 11, 12, 13.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 3 extra crabs

teach.ask: Gappu: There are so many shells! How can I count them quickly?
teach.praise: Wow! Make equal groups and count group by group. So fast!
teach.nudge: Should I put them in groups? Must every group be the same size?

learn.hook: Hop like a frog! Skip one number each time: 2, 4, 6, 8!
points: Counting by 2s means adding 2 each time.
2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 ... we jump over one number.
We count eyes, ears, shoes and wheels of a cycle by 2s.
Counting by 2s is faster than counting one by one.

example.q: There are 5 pairs of shoes outside the beach hut. How many shoes?

learn.reallife: We count shoes at the temple door or wheels of cycles by 2s.

games.title: Frog hops
games.prompt: Put them in order, counting by 2s

quiz.q: Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, ___. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Add 2 each time. 8 + 2 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1 instead of 2

quiz.q: Joseph counts slippers by 2s: 10, 12, 14, ___?
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1, or jumps by 4

quiz.q: 5 children sit on the sand. Count their eyes by 2s. How many eyes?
quiz.explain: Each child has 2 eyes. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts children, not eyes

quiz.q: Which number is missing? 20, 22, ___, 26
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1

quiz.q: Riya counts by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 9. Which number is wrong?
quiz.explain: After 6 comes 6 + 2 = 8, not 9. So 9 is wrong.
quiz.mistake: Does not check that each jump is 2

quiz.q: There are 4 cycles. Each cycle has 2 wheels. How many wheels?
quiz.explain: Count by 2s for 4 cycles: 2, 4, 6, 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 2 instead of counting 2 for each cycle

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I count by 2s? Show me!
teach.praise: Yes! Add 2 every time: 2, 4, 6, 8. Hop hop!
teach.nudge: How many do I add each time I hop?

learn.hook: One hand has 5 fingers. Two hands have 10. Let's count big numbers fast!
points: Counting by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 ... add 5 each time.
Numbers we say when counting by 5s end in 5 or 0.
Counting by 10s: 10, 20, 30 ... add 10 each time.
Numbers we say when counting by 10s end in 0.

example.q: Harpreet has 4 bags. Each bag has 10 sea shells. How many shells?

learn.reallife: We count ₹10 coins or fingers on many hands by 10s and 5s.

quiz.explain: Add 5 each time. 15 + 5 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1 instead of 5

quiz.explain: Add 10 each time. 30 + 10 = 40.
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: Aisha has 6 coins of ₹10. How much money is that?
quiz.explain: Count by 10s six times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 and 10 instead of counting by 10s

quiz.q: 4 friends hold up one hand each. Count the fingers by 5s.
quiz.explain: One hand has 5 fingers. 5, 10, 15, 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 5, or counts one hand too many

quiz.q: Which number is missing? 35, 40, ___, 50
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1, or skips one number too many

quiz.q: Count back by 10s: 90, 80, 70, ___
quiz.explain: Going back, take away 10 each time. 70 − 10 = 60.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 1 instead of 10

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I count by 10s? And by 5s?
teach.praise: Super! 10, 20, 30 and 5, 10, 15. Big jumps!
teach.nudge: How many do I add each time when I count by 5s? And by 10s?

learn.hook: A laddoo, a dice and a birthday cap. They all have shape names!
points: A sphere is round like a ball or a laddoo.
A cube is like a dice. All its faces are squares.
A cuboid is like a brick or a matchbox.
A cylinder is like a juice can or a drum.
A cone is like a birthday cap or an ice-cream cone.

example.q: Arjun sees a football, a brick and a juice can. Name their shapes.
steps: A football is round all over. It is a sphere.
A brick is like a box. It is a cuboid.
A juice can has round ends. It is a cylinder.

learn.reallife: Look in your kitchen. A gas cylinder, a sugar box and a round laddoo are all solid shapes.

games.title: Match the thing to its shape

quiz.q: A cricket ball looks like which shape?
quiz.explain: A ball is round all over, like a sphere.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a sphere with a cylinder, which has flat ends

quiz.q: A dice is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A dice has 6 faces and all of them are equal squares. That is a cube.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every box shape is a cuboid

quiz.q: Riya wears a party cap on her birthday. Its shape is a ___.
quiz.explain: A party cap has a round bottom and a pointed tip. That is a cone.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a cone with a cylinder because both have a round face

quiz.q: A brick is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A brick is a long box with flat faces. That is a cuboid.
quiz.mistake: Calls a cuboid a cube even though its faces are not all equal squares

quiz.q: A can of juice is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A can has a round top, a round bottom and a curved side. That is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a cylinder with a cone

quiz.q: Which one is NOT shaped like a sphere?
quiz.explain: A matchbox has flat faces and corners. It is a cuboid, not a sphere.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the word NOT

teach.ask: Gappu: What shape is a ball? And what shape is a dice?
teach.praise: Yes! A ball is a sphere and a dice is a cube. You know your shapes!
teach.nudge: What is the name of the round shape like a ball? And the dice shape?

learn.hook: Push a ball and it rolls away. Push a brick and it just slides. Why?
points: A sphere is curved all over. It rolls.
A cube and a cuboid have flat faces. They slide and do not roll.
A cylinder can roll on its curved side and slide on its flat face.
Shapes with flat faces are easy to stack, one on top of another.

example.q: Kabir has a ball, a dice and a can. Which one can roll and also slide?
steps: The ball has no flat face. It rolls.
The dice has only flat faces. It slides.
The can has flat ends and a curved side. It can do both.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers stack boxes and cans on shelves, but keep oranges in a basket so they do not roll away.

games.title: True or false?
items: A ball is curved all over, so it rolls.
A brick rolls down a slope easily.
A brick has flat faces. It slides, it does not roll.
A cylinder can roll and also slide.
It rolls on its curved side and slides on its flat face.
We can stack cubes to make a tower.
Cubes have flat faces, so they sit well on each other.
A sphere has a flat face.
A sphere is curved all over. It has no flat face.

quiz.q: Which shape rolls but has no flat face to slide on?
quiz.explain: A sphere is curved all over. It has no flat face at all.
quiz.mistake: Picks the cylinder, which does have two flat faces

quiz.q: Which shape can roll and also slide?
quiz.explain: A cylinder rolls on its curved side and slides on its flat face.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only one thing can happen for each shape

quiz.q: Meena wants to build a tall tower. Which shapes are best?
quiz.explain: Cubes have flat faces on top and bottom, so they stay on each other.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that round shapes roll off

quiz.q: Why does a cube not roll?
quiz.explain: A cube has no curved side. All its faces are flat, so it slides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks size or weight decides rolling

quiz.q: Kabir stands a can on its flat end and pushes it. What will it do?
quiz.explain: It is standing on its flat face, so it slides. It rolls only on its curved side.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder always rolls

quiz.q: Which one will roll down a slope?
quiz.explain: A laddoo is round like a sphere, so it rolls. The others have flat faces.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice which thing is round

teach.ask: Gappu: Why does my ball roll away but my toy brick just slides?
teach.praise: Now I see! Curved shapes roll and flat faces slide.
teach.nudge: What is different about the ball and the brick? Is it round or flat?

learn.hook: Touch a dice. Flat parts, sharp lines and pointy tips! Each has a name.
points: A face is a flat side of a shape.
An edge is the line where two faces meet.
A corner is the pointy part where edges meet.
A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A cuboid, like a matchbox, also has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A sphere has no flat face, no edge and no corner.

example.q: How many faces does a dice have?

learn.reallife: Run your finger along a box. The sharp line you feel is an edge.

games.title: Match the shape to its faces
pairs: 1 round flat face and a tip

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a cube have?
quiz.explain: Top, bottom, front, back, left and right. That is 6 faces.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the faces that can be seen at one time

quiz.q: How many edges does a cube have?
quiz.explain: 4 edges on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 standing up. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up edges with faces or corners

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has a flat circle on top and one at the bottom. Its side is curved.
quiz.mistake: Counts the curved side as a flat face

quiz.q: Which shape has no flat face, no edge and no corner?
quiz.explain: A sphere is curved all over. It has nothing flat or pointy.
quiz.mistake: Picks the cone, which has a flat face and a tip

quiz.q: A cone has how many flat faces?
quiz.explain: A cone has one flat circle at the bottom. The rest is curved up to the tip.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a cone with a cylinder, which has 2 flat faces

quiz.q: Each face of a cube is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: All 6 faces of a cube are equal squares.
quiz.mistake: Does not look closely at the flat faces

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a face? What is an edge? I am confused!
teach.praise: Hooray! A face is flat, an edge is where faces meet, and a corner is pointy.
teach.nudge: Can you tell me about the corners too? Where do the edges meet?

learn.hook: From 1 to 100! Can you climb the number ladder to the top?
points: The number just after is 1 more. After 49 comes 50.
The number just before is 1 less. Before 70 comes 69.
The number between 37 and 39 is 38.
After 99 comes 100. We read it as one hundred.
Number names: 64 is sixty-four, 70 is seventy.

example.q: Which numbers come just before and just after 60?

learn.reallife: Seat numbers on a train go 1, 2, 3 and up. House numbers on a street are in order too.

quiz.q: Which number comes just after 49?
quiz.explain: Just after means 1 more. 49 + 1 = 50.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number just before, or adds 10

quiz.q: Which number comes just before 70?
quiz.explain: Just before means 1 less. 70 − 1 = 69.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number just after instead

quiz.q: Which number is between 37 and 39?
quiz.explain: 37, 38, 39. The number in the middle is 38.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number outside the two numbers

quiz.q: How do we write sixty-four in numbers?
quiz.explain: Sixty is 6 tens and four is 4 ones. So it is 64.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the tens and ones, or writes 60 and 4 side by side

quiz.q: What comes just after 99?
quiz.explain: 99 + 1 = 100. We read it as one hundred.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the count stops at 99

quiz.q: Joseph counts train coaches: 21, 22, 23, ___, 25. Which is missing?
quiz.explain: Counting on by 1: 23 + 1 = 24. Then 24 + 1 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Skips a number or swaps the digits

teach.ask: Gappu: What number comes just after 49? How do you know?
teach.praise: Yes! Just after means one more. 49 and one more is 50.
teach.nudge: How much more is the number just after?

learn.hook: Tie 10 sticks into a bundle. Now counting is super quick!
points: 10 ones make 1 ten.
In 47, the 4 means 4 tens and the 7 means 7 ones.
The tens digit is on the left. The ones digit is on the right.

example.q: Aisha has 5 bundles of 10 sticks and 3 loose sticks. How many sticks?

learn.reallife: ₹10 notes are like tens and ₹1 coins are like ones when you count money.

quiz.q: How many tens are there in 58?
quiz.explain: In 58, the 5 is in the tens place. So there are 5 tens and 8 ones.
quiz.mistake: Picks the ones digit instead of the tens digit

quiz.q: Riya has 3 bundles of 10 sticks and 6 loose sticks. How many sticks?
quiz.explain: 3 tens is 30. 30 and 6 ones make 36.
quiz.mistake: Writes the ones first, or adds 3 and 6

quiz.q: What is the ones digit in 72?
quiz.explain: The ones digit is on the right. In 72 it is 2.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the tens digit and the ones digit

quiz.q: 4 tens and 0 ones make ___.
quiz.explain: 4 tens is 10, 20, 30, 40. With 0 ones, it is 40.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the 0 holds the ones place

quiz.q: Which is the same as 65?
quiz.explain: 65 has 6 in the tens place and 5 in the ones place.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: Arjun has 2 notes of ₹10 and 7 coins of ₹1. How much money?
quiz.explain: 2 tens is ₹20. ₹20 and ₹7 make ₹27.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 and 7, or writes 20 and 7 side by side

teach.ask: Gappu: What does the 4 mean in 47?
teach.praise: Wow! 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones. That is 40 and 7!
teach.nudge: Is the 4 telling us tens or ones? And what about the 7?

learn.hook: Who has more laddoos? Let's find out with the hungry crocodile sign!
points: Look at the tens first. More tens means a bigger number.
If the tens are the same, look at the ones.
> means greater than. < means less than. = means equal.
The open mouth of > or < always faces the bigger number.

example.q: Compare 46 and 43.

learn.reallife: We compare scores in cricket and prices in the market to see which is more.

games.title: True or false?
items: Both have 4 tens, but 8 ones is more than 0 ones. So 48 > 40.
75 has 7 tens and 57 has 5 tens. They are not equal.
To compare 52 and 25, we look at the tens first.
The tens tell us more. 5 tens is more than 2 tens.

quiz.q: Which number is bigger: 45 or 54?
quiz.explain: 54 has 5 tens. 45 has only 4 tens. So 54 is bigger.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit first

quiz.q: Which sign goes in the gap? 67 ___ 76
quiz.explain: 67 has 6 tens and 76 has 7 tens. 67 is less, so 67 < 76.
quiz.mistake: Points the open mouth at the smaller number

quiz.q: Meena scored 38 runs. Kabir scored 35 runs. Who scored more?
quiz.explain: Both have 3 tens. 8 ones is more than 5 ones, so 38 > 35.
quiz.mistake: Stops after seeing the tens are the same

quiz.q: Which is the smallest: 29, 92, 20 or 90?
quiz.explain: 29 and 20 have the fewest tens. 0 ones is less than 9 ones, so 20 is smallest.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a number with 0 at the end is always big

quiz.q: Which sign goes in the gap? 50 ___ 50
quiz.explain: Both numbers are the same, so they are equal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one side must always be bigger

quiz.q: Which number is greater than 81 but less than 85?
quiz.explain: 81, 82, 83, 84, 85. Only 83 is in the options and between them.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the two rules

teach.ask: Gappu: Is 45 bigger or 54 bigger? How do I check?
teach.praise: Brilliant! Look at the tens first. 54 has more tens, so it is bigger.
teach.nudge: Which digit should I look at first, the tens or the ones?

topics.title: Flat shapes from shadows and tracing

learn.hook: Put a can on paper and draw around it. Surprise! A flat shape appears.
points: A shadow is flat. It shows a flat shape.
Draw around the face of a solid shape to get a flat shape.
The bottom of a can or a glass gives a circle.
A face of a dice gives a square. The long face of a brick gives a rectangle.
A party cap seen from the side makes a triangle shadow.

example.q: Harpreet puts a matchbox on paper on its big face and draws around it. What shape does she get?
steps: The big face of a matchbox is long and flat.
It has 4 straight sides and 4 corners.
Two sides are long and two are short.

learn.reallife: At night, make hand shadows on the wall with a torch. Shadows are flat pictures.

games.title: What shape will you get?
pairs: Side shadow of a party cap

games.title: True or false?
items: A shadow lies flat on the wall or the floor.
Drawing around a face of a dice gives a square.
Every face of a dice is a square.
A ball has a flat face we can draw around.
A ball is curved all over. It has no flat face.
Drawing around the bottom of a glass gives a triangle.
The bottom of a glass is round, so we get a circle.

quiz.q: Riya draws around the bottom of a juice can. What shape does she get?
quiz.explain: The bottom of a can is round. Drawing around it gives a circle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of the side of the can, not its bottom

quiz.q: Arjun draws around one face of a dice. What shape does he get?
quiz.explain: Every face of a dice has 4 equal sides. That is a square.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the solid cube with its flat face

quiz.q: Meena draws around the long face of a brick. What shape does she get?
quiz.explain: The long face has 2 long sides and 2 short sides. That is a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Calls every 4-sided shape a square

quiz.q: Kabir shines a torch on a ball. What shape is its shadow on the wall?
quiz.explain: A ball is round, so its shadow is a round circle.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without thinking of the ball's round shape

quiz.q: Which solid shape can make a triangle shadow from the side?
quiz.explain: A party cap is a cone. From the side it has a pointed top and a flat bottom, like a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a dice can make a triangle

quiz.q: Which thing has a face you can draw around to get a square?
quiz.explain: A dice is a cube. Each of its faces is a square.
quiz.mistake: Picks a round object that gives a circle

teach.ask: Gappu: I drew around the bottom of a can. Why did I get a circle?
teach.praise: Yes! The flat bottom of a can is round, so it makes a circle.
teach.nudge: What shape is the flat bottom of the can?

learn.hook: A bangle, a roti and a samosa! Which ones are circles?
points: A circle is round. It has no straight sides and no corners.
A triangle has 3 straight sides.
A triangle has 3 corners.
A bangle and a coin look like circles. A samosa looks like a triangle.

example.q: How many sides and corners do 2 triangles have in all?

learn.reallife: A roti and a wheel are round like circles. A slice of pizza looks like a triangle.

quiz.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
quiz.explain: Tri means three. A triangle has 3 straight sides.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a triangle with a square

quiz.q: How many corners does a circle have?
quiz.explain: A circle is round all the way. It has no corners at all.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the start of the drawing is a corner

quiz.q: A samosa lying flat on a plate looks like a ___.
quiz.explain: A samosa has 3 pointy corners and 3 sides, like a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Does not count the corners

quiz.q: Which of these looks like a circle?
quiz.explain: A bangle is round with no corners, like a circle.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape that has corners

quiz.q: Aisha drew a shape with 3 straight sides. What did she draw?
quiz.explain: A shape with 3 straight sides is a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any shape with straight sides is a square

quiz.q: How many corners do 2 triangles have in all?
quiz.explain: Each triangle has 3 corners. 3 + 3 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts the corners of only one triangle

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I tell a circle from a triangle?
teach.praise: Super! A circle is round with no corners. A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.
teach.nudge: How many sides does a triangle have? Does a circle have corners?

learn.hook: A carrom board and a classroom door both have 4 sides. But they look different!
points: A square has 4 sides. All 4 sides are the same length.
A square has 4 corners.
A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners too.
In a rectangle, sides facing each other are the same. A door has 2 long and 2 short sides.

example.q: Kabir counts the corners on 1 square and 1 triangle. How many corners in all?

learn.reallife: A carrom board is a square. A door, a blackboard and a train ticket are rectangles.

quiz.q: How many sides does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 straight sides, all the same length.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a square with a triangle

quiz.q: What is special about the 4 sides of a square?
options: They are all the same length
quiz.explain: All 4 sides of a square are equal. That is what makes it a square.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a square with a rectangle like a door

quiz.q: A classroom door looks like a ___.
quiz.explain: A door has 4 sides: 2 long and 2 short. That is a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Calls every 4-sided shape a square

quiz.q: How many corners does a rectangle have?
quiz.explain: A rectangle has 4 corners, one at each end of its sides.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the corners on one side

quiz.q: Joseph plays carrom. The carrom board looks like a ___.
quiz.explain: A carrom board has 4 equal sides and 4 corners. It is a square.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of the round carrom pieces instead of the board

quiz.q: How many corners do 1 square and 1 triangle have in all?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 corners and a triangle has 3. 4 + 3 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks both shapes have 4 corners

teach.ask: Gappu: A square and a rectangle both have 4 sides. How are they different?
teach.praise: Now I know! A square has 4 equal sides. A rectangle has 2 long and 2 short sides.
teach.nudge: Are all the sides the same length in both? Which one has long and short sides?

learn.hook: Draw a line with a ruler. Now draw a rainbow. Are they the same?
points: A straight line does not bend. It goes the same way all along.
A curved line bends, like a rainbow or a smile.
We draw straight lines with a ruler.
Some letters have both kinds. The letter D has 1 straight line and 1 curved line.

example.q: How many straight lines and curved lines are in the letter D?
steps: The left side of D does not bend. That is 1 straight line.
The right side bends round. That is 1 curved line.

learn.reallife: The edge of a ruler is straight. A bangle and the rim of a plate are curved.

games.title: True or false?
items: A rainbow looks like a curved line.
A rainbow bends like a big arch.
We use a ruler to draw a curved line.
A ruler helps us draw straight lines.
The letter O has no straight line.
O is one round curved line.
The letter L has a curved line.
L has 2 straight lines and no curve.
The letter D has a straight line and a curved line.
Its left side is straight and its right side is curved.

quiz.q: Which letter has only straight lines?
quiz.explain: T is made of 2 straight lines. O, C and S are curved.
quiz.mistake: Does not look for bends in the letters

quiz.q: How many straight lines are in the letter T?
quiz.explain: T has 1 line on top and 1 line going down. That is 2 lines.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the line going down

quiz.q: Which shape is made of only one curved line?
quiz.explain: A circle is one round line that bends all the way. It has no straight lines.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up shapes with straight sides and round shapes

quiz.q: How many straight lines are in the letter E?
quiz.explain: E has 1 standing line on the left and 3 short lines going right. 1 + 3 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the standing line on the left

quiz.q: Meena draws a smile on a face. What kind of line is a smile?
quiz.explain: A smile bends like a little bowl. So it is a curved line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every line is straight

quiz.q: How many curved lines are in the letter B?
quiz.explain: B has 1 straight line and 2 round bumps. Each bump is a curved line.
quiz.mistake: Counts the two bumps as one curve

teach.ask: Gappu: What is the difference between a straight line and a curved line?
teach.praise: I get it! A straight line does not bend. A curved line bends like a rainbow.
teach.nudge: Which line bends? Which line can I draw with a ruler?

learn.hook: A flagpole stands up. A sleepy cat lies flat. A slide leans. Lines can do this too!
points: A sleeping line goes from left to right, like the floor. It is a horizontal line.
A standing line goes up and down, like a flagpole. It is a vertical line.
A slanting line leans to one side, like a slide in the park.
The letter H has 2 standing lines and 1 sleeping line.

example.q: Look at the letter A. What lines does it have?
steps: The two sides lean in. They are 2 slanting lines.
The middle line lies flat. It is 1 sleeping line.

learn.reallife: The legs of a table are standing lines. The table top is a sleeping line. A slide is slanting.

games.title: Match the letter to its lines

quiz.q: A flagpole is a ___ line.
quiz.explain: A flagpole goes straight up and down. That is a standing line.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up standing and sleeping lines

quiz.q: Which line is like the floor of your room?
quiz.explain: The floor lies flat from left to right. That is a sleeping line.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up standing and sleeping lines

quiz.q: A slide in the park is a ___ line.
quiz.explain: A slide leans to one side. It is not straight up and not flat. So it is slanting.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a line can only stand or sleep

quiz.q: How many standing lines are in the letter H?
quiz.explain: H has a standing line on the left and one on the right. The middle line is sleeping.
quiz.mistake: Counts the sleeping middle line too

quiz.q: How many slanting lines are in the letter W?
quiz.explain: W goes down, up, down, up. Each part leans. That is 4 slanting lines.
quiz.mistake: Thinks W is made of 2 lines like V

quiz.q: Which letter has only standing and sleeping lines?
quiz.explain: L has 1 standing line and 1 sleeping line. A, V and X have slanting lines.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the leaning lines in A, V and X

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a standing line? A sleeping line? And a slanting line?
teach.praise: Wow! Standing goes up and down, sleeping lies flat, and slanting leans. Perfect!
teach.nudge: Which line goes up like a flagpole? Which one lies flat? Which one leans?

learn.hook: A rangoli is full of lines! Straight, curved, standing and slanting. Let's count them.
points: A pattern repeats the same lines again and again.
A square has 4 straight lines: 2 standing and 2 sleeping.
A tent shape has 2 slanting lines and 1 sleeping line.
A circle is made of 1 curved line.

example.q: Arjun draws 3 squares that do not touch. How many straight lines?

learn.reallife: Rangoli, kite strings, window bars and railway tracks all show lines.

items.q: Straight lines in the letter L
Straight lines in the letter H
Curved lines in the letter O

quiz.q: Meena draws a square. How many sleeping lines does it have?
quiz.explain: The top and the bottom of a square are sleeping lines. The two sides are standing lines.
quiz.mistake: Counts all 4 sides as sleeping lines

quiz.q: Kabir draws 2 triangles that do not touch. How many straight lines in all?
quiz.explain: Each triangle has 3 straight lines. 3 + 3 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts the lines of only one triangle

quiz.q: Which pattern repeats a curved line?
quiz.explain: ( bends, so it is a curved line. | and — are straight.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice which mark bends

quiz.q: What comes next? / \ / \ / ___
quiz.explain: The lines take turns: /, then \. After / comes \.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that the two lines take turns

quiz.q: Joseph makes a rangoli with 4 circles. How many curved lines?
quiz.explain: Each circle is 1 curved line. 4 circles make 4 curved lines.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a circle has no lines

quiz.q: Aisha draws 2 squares and 1 triangle, none touching. How many straight lines?
quiz.explain: Squares: 4 + 4 = 8. Triangle: 3. 8 + 3 = 11.
quiz.mistake: Counts 4 lines for the triangle too

teach.ask: Gappu: How many straight lines are in a square? How do you count them?
teach.praise: Yes! A square has 4 straight sides. Count them: 1, 2, 3, 4!
teach.nudge: How many sides does a square have? Are they straight or curved?

learn.hook: Diwali is here! Riya has 24 diyas and Arjun has 13. How many diyas can they light?
points: Add the ones first. Then add the tens.
If the ones make 10 or more, make a new ten.
Carry the new ten to the tens place and add it there.

example.q: Meena has 36 flowers. She gets 27 more. How many flowers now?
steps: Ones: 6 + 7 = 13. That is 1 ten and 3 ones.
Write 3 in the ones. Carry 1 ten.

learn.reallife: We add when we count sweets in two boxes or runs made in two overs.

quiz.q: Riya has 24 diyas. Arjun has 13 diyas. How many diyas in all?
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: What is 52 + 30?
quiz.explain: 30 is 3 tens. 5 tens and 3 tens make 8 tens. The 2 ones stay. So 82.
quiz.mistake: Adds the 3 to the ones instead of the tens

quiz.q: Kabir has 36 balloons. He buys 27 more. How many balloons now?
quiz.explain: Ones: 6 + 7 = 13. Write 3 and carry 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. So 63.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry the new ten

quiz.q: What is 45 + 8?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry, or writes 13 in the ones place

quiz.q: Fill the gap: 40 + ___ = 70
quiz.explain: From 40, count on by 10s: 50, 60, 70. That is 3 tens, or 30.
quiz.mistake: Writes 3 instead of 3 tens, or adds 40 and 70

quiz.q: Which sum is equal to 50?
quiz.mistake: Picks a sum that has 50 in it without adding

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I add 24 and 13?
teach.praise: Super! Add the ones first, then the tens. 24 + 13 = 37!
teach.nudge: Which do I add first, the ones or the tens?

learn.hook: Harpreet made 45 laddoos. Her friends ate 12. How many are left?
points: Take away the ones first. Then take away the tens.
If the top ones digit is too small, break 1 ten into 10 ones.
Check by adding: 33 + 12 = 45.

example.q: Joseph has 52 marbles. He gives away 27. How many are left?
steps: Break 1 ten. Now there are 4 tens and 12 ones.

learn.reallife: We take away to find how many sweets are left or how much money we get back.

games.title: True or false?
items: 5 tens take away 2 tens leaves 3 tens.
Adding back the part we took away gives the first number.
In 52 − 27, we can just do 7 − 2 in the ones.
We must take 7 from 2. 2 is too small, so we break a ten first.

quiz.q: Harpreet made 45 laddoos. Her friends ate 12. How many laddoos are left?
quiz.explain: Ones: 5 − 2 = 3. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3. So 33 are left.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away

quiz.q: What is 80 − 30?
quiz.explain: 8 tens take away 3 tens leaves 5 tens. 5 tens is 50.
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers, or forgets the 0 in the ones

quiz.q: What is 52 − 27?
quiz.explain: 2 is too small to take 7. Break a ten: 12 − 7 = 5. Then 4 tens − 2 tens = 2 tens. So 25.
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller ones digit from the bigger one (7 − 2) instead of breaking a ten

quiz.q: Aisha had 30 bangles. She gave 8 to her sister. How many does Aisha have now?
quiz.explain: Count back 8 from 30: 29, 28, 27, 26, 25, 24, 23, 22. So 22 are left.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away, or counts 30 itself while counting back

quiz.q: Fill the gap: 90 − ___ = 50
quiz.explain: From 90 go back by 10s to 50: 80, 70, 60, 50. That is 4 tens, or 40.
quiz.mistake: Writes 4 instead of 4 tens, or adds the numbers

quiz.q: Kabir has 61 stickers. He uses 25. How many stickers are left?
quiz.explain: 1 is too small to take 5. Break a ten: 11 − 5 = 6. Then 5 tens − 2 tens = 3 tens. So 36.
quiz.mistake: Does 5 − 1 in the ones, or forgets that one ten was broken

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I take 12 away from 45?
teach.praise: Yes! Take away the ones, then the tens. 45 − 12 = 33!
teach.nudge: What do I take away first, the ones or the tens?

learn.hook: Is it a 'put together' story or a 'take away' story? Find the clue word!
points: Read the story. Find the numbers.
Words like 'in all' and 'altogether' tell us to add.
Words like 'left', 'gave away' and 'ate' tell us to take away.
'How many more' means find the difference. Take the small number from the big one.
Check: does the answer make sense?

example.q: There are 48 marigold flowers. Meena uses 23 for a garland. How many are left?

learn.reallife: At the market, at a party or in a cricket match, we solve stories like these.

games.title: Add or take away?
items: Riya has 12 diyas and buys 5 more. How many in all?
There were 20 balloons. 6 burst. How many are left?
Arjun ate 3 of his 10 laddoos. How many are left?
8 boys and 9 girls play. How many children altogether?
Kabir gave away 7 of his 15 cards. How many are left?
A train has 30 people. 10 more get on. How many now?

quiz.q: A rangoli has 25 red dots and 32 yellow dots. How many dots in all?
quiz.explain: 'In all' means add. Ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Tens: 2 + 3 = 5. So 57.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: There were 40 sweets in a box. The guests ate 18. How many sweets are left?
quiz.explain: 'Left' means take away. 0 is too small to take 8, so break a ten: 10 − 8 = 2. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. So 22.
quiz.mistake: Does 8 − 0 in the ones instead of breaking a ten

quiz.q: Joseph's team scored 46 runs. The other team scored 38. How many more runs did Joseph's team score?
quiz.explain: 'How many more' means take the small number from the big one. 46 − 38 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds the scores, or does 8 − 6 in the ones

quiz.q: A train has 54 people. At a station, 21 get off. How many are on the train now?
quiz.explain: People got off, so take away. Ones: 4 − 1 = 3. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. So 33.
quiz.mistake: Adds the people who got off

quiz.q: Aisha buys a pencil for ₹15 and an eraser for ₹7. How much does she pay?
quiz.explain: She pays for both, so add. ₹15 + ₹5 = ₹20. Then 2 more makes ₹22.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding, or forgets to carry

quiz.q: Which word in a story tells you to take away?
quiz.explain: 'Left' asks what remains after some are gone. So we take away.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every story needs adding

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know if a story needs adding or taking away?
teach.praise: Clever! 'In all' means add and 'left' means take away. I will look for clue words!
teach.nudge: Which clue words tell me to add? Which words tell me to take away?

learn.hook: How long is your table? You can measure it with your own hand!
points: A hand-span goes from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger. Spread the hand wide.
We measure small things like a table with hand-spans.
We measure big things like a room with steps.
Longer things need more spans or steps.
People get different answers. A bigger hand needs fewer spans.

example.q: Riya's table is 6 of her hand-spans long. Her father's hand is bigger. Will he count more or fewer spans?
steps: Father's span is longer than Riya's.
Each long span covers more of the table.

learn.reallife: In gully cricket, children measure the pitch with steps. Tailors and carpenters measure too.

games.title: True or false?
items: A room is easier to measure in steps than in hand-spans.
A room is big. Steps are longer, so we count fewer.
Everyone's hand-span is the same size.
Hands are different sizes, so spans are different too.
With the same hand, a longer thing needs more hand-spans.
More length to cover means more spans.
A big hand needs more spans than a small hand for the same table.
A big span covers more, so it needs fewer spans.
We spread the hand wide to make a hand-span.
A span goes from the thumb tip to the little finger tip.

quiz.q: Arjun's book is 2 hand-spans long. His table is 7 hand-spans long. Which is longer?
quiz.explain: The table needs 7 spans and the book needs only 2. More spans means longer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a smaller number of spans means longer

quiz.q: Meena's mat is 5 spans long. Her rope is 9 spans long. How many spans longer is the rope?
quiz.explain: Find the difference. 9 − 5 = 4. The rope is 4 spans longer.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two lengths instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: What is the best way to measure the length of your classroom?
quiz.explain: A classroom is big. Steps are long, so counting is quick.
quiz.mistake: Picks a small unit that takes too long for a big room

quiz.q: Kabir walks across a room in 12 steps. His dad does it in 8 steps. Why?
quiz.explain: Dad's steps are longer. Longer steps cover the room in fewer steps.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the room changed size

quiz.q: A table is 4 hand-spans long. Two such tables are put end to end. How many hand-spans long are they?
quiz.explain: Each table is 4 spans. 4 + 4 = 8 spans.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one table

quiz.q: Harpreet walks 6 steps to the door and 6 more steps to the gate. How many steps in all?
quiz.explain: Add the two parts. 6 + 6 = 12 steps.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one part of the walk

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I measure my table without a ruler?
teach.praise: Great idea! I will put my hand-span again and again and count. No ruler needed!
teach.nudge: What part of my body can I use? What do I do after I place it?

learn.hook: A pillow is big but light. A small stone is heavy! Size does not always tell weight.
points: Hold one thing in each hand. Feel which one pulls down more. That is heavier.
On a balance or a see-saw, the heavier side goes down.
The lighter side goes up.
A big thing is not always heavy. A balloon is big but light.

example.q: On a balance, a bag of rice goes down. A bag of puffed rice goes up. Which is heavier?

learn.reallife: The vegetable seller weighs onions on a balance. On a see-saw, the heavier child goes down.

quiz.q: Which one is the heaviest?
quiz.explain: A brick is hard and solid. It is much heavier than a feather or a leaf.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how things feel when we lift them

quiz.q: On a see-saw, Arjun goes down and Riya goes up. Who is heavier?
quiz.explain: The heavier side of a see-saw goes down. Arjun went down.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the side that goes up is heavier

quiz.q: A big balloon and a small stone. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: The balloon is full of air and is very light. The small stone is heavier.
quiz.mistake: Thinks bigger things are always heavier

quiz.q: On a balance, 1 melon weighs the same as 6 apples. 2 such melons weigh the same as how many apples?
quiz.explain: Each melon is 6 apples. 2 melons are 6 + 6 = 12 apples.
quiz.mistake: Forgets there are 2 melons

quiz.q: A pencil balances 3 ₹1 coins. A pen balances 5 ₹1 coins. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: The pen needs 5 coins to balance. 5 is more than 3, so the pen is heavier.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fewer coins means heavier

quiz.q: A bag of onions balances 10 blocks. A bag of potatoes balances 14 blocks. How many more blocks for the potatoes?
quiz.explain: Find the difference. 14 − 10 = 4 more blocks.
quiz.mistake: Adds the blocks instead of finding the difference

teach.ask: Gappu: My balloon is big. So it must be heavy, right?
teach.praise: Oh! Big things can be light. I should lift them or use a balance to check.
teach.nudge: Is a big thing always heavy? How can I check which is heavier?

learn.hook: A bucket, a jug and a glass. Which one holds the most water?
points: Capacity means how much a thing can hold.
A bucket holds more water than a glass.
We can measure with a cup: how many cups fill the jug?
The one that needs more cups to fill holds more.
A tall thing does not always hold more. Pour and check.

example.q: A jug fills 5 glasses. A bottle fills 3 glasses. Which holds more?

learn.reallife: Mummy uses a cup to measure water for rice. Milk comes in packets and bottles.

games.title: Holds least to most
games.prompt: Holds the least water to holds the most

quiz.q: Which one holds the most water?
quiz.explain: A bucket is much bigger inside. It can fill many cups.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how much fits inside

quiz.q: A jug fills 6 glasses. A bottle fills 4 glasses. How many more glasses does the jug fill?
quiz.explain: Find the difference. 6 − 4 = 2 more glasses.
quiz.mistake: Adds the glasses instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: A pot fills 3 jugs. Each jug fills 5 glasses. How many glasses does the pot fill?
quiz.explain: 3 jugs of 5 glasses each. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 5 instead of counting 3 groups of 5

quiz.q: Using the same cup, Kabir fills his bottle with 4 cups. Joseph fills his with 7 cups. Whose bottle holds more?
quiz.explain: Joseph's bottle takes 7 cups. 7 is more than 4, so it holds more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fewer cups means it holds more

quiz.q: What does capacity mean?
options: How much a thing can hold
quiz.explain: Capacity tells how much water, milk or sand a thing can hold.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up capacity with weight or length

quiz.q: A bucket holds 10 mugs of water. Meena has poured in 6 mugs. How many more mugs to fill it?
quiz.explain: Count up from 6 to 10: 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 4 more mugs.
quiz.mistake: Adds the mugs instead of finding what is missing

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I find which bottle holds more water?
teach.praise: Yes! Fill each one with cups and count. More cups means it holds more!
teach.nudge: What can I pour with? What do I count?

learn.hook: 4 plates with 3 laddoos on each. Fair for everyone! These are equal groups.
points: Equal groups have the same number in each group.
3 plates with 2 laddoos on each are equal groups.
If one plate has more, the groups are not equal.
We say: 3 groups of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6.

example.q: Riya puts 4 pencils in each of 3 boxes. Are these equal groups? How many pencils?
steps: Each box has 4. So the groups are equal.

learn.reallife: Eggs sit in a tray in equal rows. Bangles are sold in sets of the same size.

games.title: Equal or not?
items: Groups of 2, 2 and 2 are equal groups.
Groups of 3, 4 and 3 are equal groups.
One group has 4. Equal groups must all be the same.
Equal groups have the same number in each group.

quiz.q: Which one shows equal groups?
quiz.explain: In 3, 3, 3 every group has 3. The others have groups of different sizes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any groups are equal groups

quiz.q: There are 5 plates. Each plate has 2 laddoos. How many laddoos?
quiz.explain: 5 groups of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 and 2 instead of counting 5 groups of 2

quiz.q: Arjun makes 3 groups of 4 marbles. How many marbles?
quiz.explain: Count by 4s for 3 groups: 4, 8, 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 4, or writes 3 and 4 side by side

quiz.q: Meena puts 12 bangles in groups of 3. How many groups does she make?
quiz.explain: Count by 3s till 12: 3, 6, 9, 12. That is 4 groups.
quiz.mistake: Gives the size of a group instead of the number of groups

quiz.q: Three plates have 4, 4 and 3 sweets. How can we make the groups equal?
options: Add 1 sweet to the last plate
Take 1 sweet from the last plate
Add 2 sweets to the first plate
quiz.explain: Add 1 to the last plate: 3 + 1 = 4. Now every plate has 4.
quiz.mistake: Changes a plate that already matches the others

quiz.q: Kabir has 4 boxes with 5 crayons in each. How many crayons?
quiz.explain: Count by 5s for 4 boxes: 5, 10, 15, 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 5, or counts one box too few or too many

teach.ask: Gappu: What are equal groups?
teach.praise: Now I know! Equal groups have the same number in each group.
teach.nudge: Does every group need the same number?

topics.title: Adding equal groups again and again

learn.hook: Adding the same number again and again? There is a quick way to say it!
points: 3 groups of 5 means 5 + 5 + 5.
We can write it as 3 × 5 = 15. We say '3 times 5'.
× means 'groups of'. 2 × 4 means 2 groups of 4.

example.q: A cycle-rickshaw has 3 wheels. How many wheels do 4 rickshaws have?

learn.reallife: We count legs of cows, wheels of autos and fingers on hands like this.

quiz.q: Which is the same as 4 + 4 + 4?
quiz.explain: There are 3 fours. 3 groups of 4 is 3 × 4.
quiz.mistake: Counts the size of the group instead of how many groups

quiz.q: A cow has 4 legs. How many legs do 3 cows have?
quiz.explain: 3 groups of 4. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 4 instead of adding 4 three times

quiz.q: What is 5 + 5 + 5 + 5?
quiz.explain: Count by 5s four times: 5, 10, 15, 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds one 5 too few or too many

quiz.q: An auto has 3 wheels. How many wheels do 5 autos have?
quiz.explain: 5 groups of 3. Count by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 and 3 instead of counting 5 groups of 3

quiz.q: 2 × 6 means ___
quiz.explain: 2 × 6 means 2 groups of 6. That is 6 + 6 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Thinks × means add the two numbers

quiz.q: Aisha has 2 Diwali boxes. Each box has 10 sweets. How many sweets?
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 and 10, or counts only one box

teach.ask: Gappu: What does 3 × 4 mean?
teach.praise: Wow! 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4. Add 4 again and again: 12!
teach.nudge: Is it groups? What number do I add again and again?

learn.hook: 6 laddoos and 2 friends. How do we share so it is fair?
points: Sharing equally means everyone gets the same.
Give one to each friend, again and again, till none are left.
12 shared by 3 friends: each gets 4.
Check by adding: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

example.q: Harpreet shares 10 bananas equally between 2 monkeys. How many does each get?
steps: Give 1 to each monkey. Keep going.
When all 10 are given, each monkey has 5.

learn.reallife: We share sweets on Diwali and split friends into equal teams for cricket.

quiz.q: Riya shares 8 laddoos equally with her brother. How many does each get?
quiz.explain: 8 shared by 2 people. 4 + 4 = 8, so each gets 4.
quiz.mistake: Takes 2 away from 8 instead of sharing

quiz.q: 15 pencils are shared equally by 3 children. How many does each child get?
quiz.explain: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. So each child gets 5.
quiz.mistake: Takes 3 away from 15 instead of sharing

quiz.q: Kabir gives away all his 12 stickers, 3 to each friend. How many friends get stickers?
quiz.explain: Make groups of 3 till 12: 3, 6, 9, 12. That is 4 friends.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number each friend gets, not the number of friends

quiz.q: 20 children make 2 equal cricket teams. How many children are in each team?
quiz.explain: 10 + 10 = 20. So each team has 10 children.
quiz.mistake: Takes 2 away from 20 instead of sharing

quiz.q: Joseph shares 7 sweets equally between 2 friends. What happens?
options: Each gets 3 and 1 is left over
Each gets 3 and 2 are left over
quiz.explain: 3 + 3 = 6. One sweet is left. 4 + 4 = 8 is too many.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every number can be shared into 2 equal parts

quiz.q: Meena gets 4 balloons. Her 2 friends get 4 balloons each too. How many balloons were shared?
quiz.explain: Meena and 2 friends make 3 children. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count Meena too

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I share 6 laddoos with my friend fairly?
teach.praise: Yes! Give one each again and again. We both get 3. Fair!
teach.nudge: Should we both get the same? How many does each of us get?

learn.hook: Sunday is fun day! But which day comes after it? Let's learn the 7 days.
points: A week has 7 days.
Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
After Saturday, a new week starts with Sunday.
Yesterday is the day before today. Tomorrow is the day after today.

example.q: Today is Wednesday. What day will it be tomorrow? What day was it yesterday?
steps: The day after Wednesday is Thursday.
The day before Wednesday is Tuesday.
example.answer: Tomorrow is Thursday. Yesterday was Tuesday.

learn.reallife: School days, the weekly market day and the Sunday holiday all follow the days of the week.

quiz.q: How many days are there in a week?
quiz.explain: Sunday to Saturday makes 7 days.
steps: Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat
quiz.mistake: Counts only the school days

quiz.q: Today is Thursday. What day is tomorrow?
quiz.explain: Tomorrow is the day after today. After Thursday comes Friday.
quiz.mistake: Gives the day before instead of the day after

quiz.q: Yesterday was Sunday. What day is today?
quiz.explain: Today is the day after yesterday. After Sunday comes Monday.
quiz.mistake: Goes back a day instead of forward

quiz.q: Arjun plays cricket every Saturday and Sunday. How many days does he play in 2 weeks?
quiz.explain: He plays 2 days each week. 2 weeks: 2 + 2 = 4 days.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one week

quiz.q: How many days are there in 2 weeks?
quiz.explain: Each week has 7 days. 7 + 7 = 14 days.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 and 7, or writes 7 and 2 side by side

quiz.q: Kabir's birthday is 3 days after Monday. Which day is it?
quiz.explain: Count 3 days on from Monday: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.
quiz.mistake: Counts Monday as one of the 3 days

teach.ask: Gappu: Today is Monday. What day is tomorrow? How do you know?
teach.praise: Yes! Tomorrow is the day after today. After Monday comes Tuesday!
teach.nudge: Does tomorrow come before today or after today?

learn.hook: Birthdays, Diwali and summer holidays! They all come in different months.
points: A year has 12 months.
January, February, March, April, May, June.
July, August, September, October, November, December.
January is the first month. December is the last month.
After December, a new year starts with January.

example.q: Which month comes just after March? Which comes just before March?
steps: The month after March is April.
The month before March is February.
example.answer: April comes after. February comes before.

learn.reallife: A calendar on the wall has one page for each of the 12 months.

quiz.q: How many months are there in a year?
quiz.explain: January to December makes 12 months.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up months in a year with days in a week

quiz.q: Which month comes just after June?
quiz.explain: The order is May, June, July. So July comes after June.
quiz.mistake: Gives the month before, or skips a month

quiz.q: Which is the first month of the year?
quiz.explain: Every year starts with January.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the first and the last month

quiz.q: Which month comes just before January?
quiz.explain: December is the last month. Then a new year starts with January.
quiz.mistake: Thinks nothing comes before January

quiz.q: Meena's birthday is in the 3rd month of the year. Which month is it?
quiz.explain: 1st January, 2nd February, 3rd March.
quiz.mistake: Counts from the wrong month

quiz.q: How many months come after September in the same year?
quiz.explain: After September come October, November and December. That is 3 months.
quiz.mistake: Counts September too

teach.ask: Gappu: How many months are in a year? Which one comes first?
teach.praise: Hooray! 12 months, and January comes first. December is last!
teach.nudge: How many months are there? What is the name of the first one?

learn.hook: Mangoes, umbrellas and sweaters! Each one belongs to a season.
points: In summer it is hot. We drink cool water and eat mangoes.
In the rainy season it rains a lot. We use umbrellas and raincoats.
In winter it is cold. We wear sweaters.
A calendar shows the days, weeks and months of a year.
Most months have 30 or 31 days. February is the shortest month.

example.q: On a calendar, the 1st of the month is a Monday. What day is the 8th?
steps: So the 8th is also a Monday.

learn.reallife: We look at the calendar to find festivals, holidays and birthdays.

games.title: True or false?
items: Winter is cold, so we wear warm clothes.
A calendar shows the days and months.
It shows every day of every month.
We use umbrellas in the rainy season.
Umbrellas keep us dry in the rain.
If the 1st is a Monday, the 8th is a Monday too.
7 days later it is the same day again.
Summer is hot. Winter is the cold one.

quiz.q: In which season do we wear sweaters?
quiz.explain: Winter is cold. Sweaters keep us warm.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up hot and cold seasons

quiz.q: Aisha carries an umbrella and makes paper boats in puddles. Which season is it?
quiz.explain: Puddles and umbrellas mean lots of rain. It is the rainy season.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clues in the story

quiz.q: On a calendar, the 1st is a Friday. What day is the 8th?
quiz.explain: The 8th is 7 days after the 1st. 7 days later is the same day: Friday.
steps: 7 days later is the same day
quiz.mistake: Moves on 1 day instead of 7 days

quiz.q: On a calendar, the 5th is a Tuesday. On which date is the next Tuesday?
quiz.explain: The next Tuesday is 7 days later. 5 + 7 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 days instead of 7, or adds 1

quiz.q: Most months have how many days?
quiz.explain: Most months have 30 or 31 days. Only February has fewer.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up days in a month with days in a week or months in a year

quiz.q: Which month is the shortest?
quiz.explain: February has only 28 days, or 29 in a leap year. Other months have 30 or 31.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all months have the same number of days

teach.ask: Gappu: What do we wear and do in each season?
teach.praise: Lovely! Mangoes in summer, umbrellas in the rain, sweaters in winter!
teach.nudge: What happens in summer? In the rainy season? In winter?

learn.hook: The fair is here! But first, let's get to know our money.
points: Indian money is the rupee. We write it as ₹.
Notes: ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100 and more.
Small coins can add up to a bigger amount. Two ₹5 coins make ₹10.

example.q: How many ₹2 coins make ₹10?
steps: We said 5 numbers. That is 5 coins.

learn.reallife: At the shop we pay with coins and notes. Your piggy bank is full of coins!

quiz.q: How many ₹1 coins make ₹10?
quiz.explain: Each coin is ₹1. Count 1 to 10. That is 10 coins.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one coin is enough for any amount

quiz.q: Riya has two ₹10 notes and one ₹5 coin. How much money does she have?
quiz.mistake: Counts only one ₹10 note, or forgets the coin

quiz.q: How many ₹5 coins make ₹20?
quiz.explain: Count by 5s till 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 coins.
quiz.mistake: Gives the value of a coin instead of the number of coins

quiz.q: Which is the most money?
quiz.explain: ₹50 is more than ₹20 and ₹10.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a coin is worth more because it is heavy

quiz.q: Arjun has one ₹50 note. Kabir has five ₹10 notes. Who has more money?
quiz.explain: Five ₹10 notes: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. That is ₹50, same as Arjun.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more notes always means more money

quiz.q: Meena has three ₹20 notes. How much money does she have?
quiz.explain: Count by 20s: 20, 40, 60. That is ₹60.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 20 instead of counting three ₹20 notes

teach.ask: Gappu: How many ₹2 coins do I need to make ₹10?
teach.praise: Yes! Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Five ₹2 coins make ₹10!
teach.nudge: Can I count by 2s up to 10? How many coins is that?

learn.hook: A balloon and a whistle! How much money do you need for both?
points: We add rupees just like numbers.
Add the notes first. Then add the coins.
Count on for ₹10 notes: ₹50, ₹60, ₹70.

example.q: Aisha has a ₹50 note, a ₹20 note and a ₹5 coin. How much money is that?

learn.reallife: At the fair we add the prices of rides and snacks to see how much to pay.

quiz.q: A balloon costs ₹15. A whistle costs ₹10. How much for both?
quiz.explain: Add the prices. ₹15 + ₹10 = ₹25.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: Kabir has a ₹50 note and a ₹20 note. How much money does he have?
quiz.explain: ₹50 + ₹20: 5 tens and 2 tens make 7 tens. That is ₹70.
quiz.mistake: Writes 50 and 20 side by side, or takes away

quiz.q: What is ₹45 + ₹27?
quiz.explain: Ones: 5 + 7 = 12. Write 2, carry 1. Tens: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. So ₹72.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry the new ten

quiz.q: Harpreet buys a toffee for ₹2, a pencil for ₹5 and a pen for ₹10. How much does she pay?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one of the three things

quiz.q: Joseph has three ₹10 coins and four ₹1 coins. How much money does he have?
quiz.explain: Three ₹10 coins make ₹30. Four ₹1 coins make ₹4. ₹30 + ₹4 = ₹34.
quiz.mistake: Adds the number of coins, or swaps tens and ones

quiz.q: Riya saves ₹20 on Monday and ₹20 on Tuesday. How much does she save in all?
quiz.explain: ₹20 + ₹20: 2 tens and 2 tens make 4 tens. That is ₹40.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

teach.ask: Gappu: I have ₹50 and ₹20. How much money is that?
teach.praise: Super! Add them up: ₹50 and ₹20 make ₹70!
teach.nudge: Should I add or take away? What do ₹50 and ₹20 make together?

learn.hook: You give the shopkeeper ₹20 for a ₹15 toy. Do you get money back?
points: The shopkeeper sells. We buy and pay.
If we pay more than the price, the shopkeeper gives money back. This is called change.
Change = money we give − price.
Pay ₹20 for a ₹15 toy: change is ₹5.

example.q: Meena buys a ribbon for ₹12. She pays with a ₹20 note. How much change does she get?

learn.reallife: At the fair, the vegetable market or the school canteen, we pay and get change.

games.title: True or false?
items: If you pay ₹10 for a ₹10 toffee packet, you get no change.
Paying ₹50 for a ₹30 book gives ₹20 change.
Paying ₹20 for a ₹14 pen gives ₹4 change.
With only ₹10 you can buy a toy that costs ₹25.
₹25 is more than ₹10. You need ₹15 more.
The shopkeeper gives change when we pay more than the price.
Change is the extra money given back.

quiz.q: A kite costs ₹15. Arjun pays ₹20. How much change does he get?
quiz.explain: Change = ₹20 − ₹15. Count up from 15 to 20: that is 5. So ₹5.
quiz.mistake: Adds the money and the price

quiz.q: Aisha has ₹30. A doll costs ₹25. Can she buy it?
quiz.explain: ₹30 is more than ₹25, so she can buy it. ₹30 − ₹25 = ₹5 change.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the money with the price

quiz.q: Kabir pays ₹50 for a toy car that costs ₹35. How much change does he get?
quiz.mistake: Does 5 − 0 in the ones instead of breaking a ten

quiz.q: Joseph has ₹40. He buys a ball for ₹18. How much money is left?
quiz.mistake: Does 8 − 0 in the ones, or forgets that one ten was broken

quiz.q: A stall sells laddoos at ₹5 each. How much for 4 laddoos?
quiz.explain: 4 laddoos at ₹5 each. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So ₹20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 5 instead of counting ₹5 four times

quiz.q: Riya wants a ₹60 bag. She has ₹45. How much more money does she need?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two amounts, or does 5 − 0 in the ones

teach.ask: Gappu: I pay ₹20 for a ₹15 toy. How much change do I get?
teach.praise: Yes! ₹20 take away ₹15 is ₹5. I get ₹5 back!
teach.nudge: How much more is ₹20 than ₹15? Should I take away?

learn.hook: Which sweet does your class like best? Let's ask and find out!
points: Data is information we collect, like the favourite fruits of our friends.
We ask a question and write down the answers.
We sort things into groups by colour, shape or kind.
Then we count each group and compare.

example.q: Riya asks 8 friends their favourite sweet. 5 say laddoo and 3 say jalebi. Which is liked more?

learn.reallife: Teachers count how many children are present. Shopkeepers count which toys sell the most.

games.title: True or false?
items: We can sort buttons by colour.
Red buttons in one group, blue in another.
Data is a kind of food.
Data is information we collect, like answers or counts.
After sorting, we count each group.
Counting tells us how many are in each group.
If 6 children like tea and 4 like milk, more children like milk.
6 is more than 4, so more children like tea.
Asking friends their favourite game is collecting data.

quiz.q: Arjun sorts 10 marbles. 6 are red and the rest are blue. How many are blue?
quiz.explain: The rest means what is left. 10 − 6 = 4 blue marbles.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the rest

quiz.q: In a class, 7 children like cricket and 5 like football. How many children in all?
quiz.explain: 'In all' means add. 7 + 5 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: 7 children like cricket and 5 like football. How many more children like cricket?
quiz.explain: 'How many more' means find the difference. 7 − 5 = 2.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two groups instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Meena puts her red toys in one box and her blue toys in another. What is she doing?
quiz.explain: Putting things into groups by colour is sorting.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word for making groups

quiz.q: Kabir asks 9 friends. 4 like mango, 3 like apple and 2 like banana. Which fruit is liked the least?
quiz.explain: Banana has only 2. That is the smallest number.
quiz.mistake: Picks the fruit liked the most

quiz.q: Aisha has 3 red, 5 yellow and 4 green bangles. How many bangles in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one colour

teach.ask: Gappu: My friends told me their favourite fruits. What do I do now?
teach.praise: Great! Sort the answers into groups and count each group. Now I know the favourite!
teach.nudge: Should I put the same answers together? Then what do I do with each group?

learn.hook: Cars zoom past the school gate. How can we keep count fast? Tally marks!
points: Make one small line | for each thing you count.
For the 5th thing, draw a line across the first 4 lines. This makes a bundle of 5.
Count the bundles by 5s. Then add the extra lines.
Tally marks help us count while things keep coming.

example.q: Kabir counts cars with tally marks. He has 2 bundles and 3 more lines. How many cars?

learn.reallife: In a cricket match, scorers can use tally marks to keep count of runs.

quiz.q: Kabir counts cars at the gate. His tally is |||. How many cars?
quiz.explain: Each line is 1. There are 3 lines, so the number is 3.
quiz.mistake: Miscounts the lines

quiz.q: How do we make a bundle of 5 in tally marks?
options: We draw a line across 4 lines
quiz.explain: We draw 4 lines. The 5th line goes across them. That is a bundle of 5.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how the 5th tally mark is drawn

quiz.q: Riya's tally shows 3 bundles. How many is that?
quiz.explain: Each bundle is 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15.
quiz.mistake: Counts bundles as 1 each, or adds 3 and 5

quiz.q: Joseph's tally shows 2 bundles and |||| (4 lines). How many is that?
quiz.explain: 2 bundles: 5, 10. Then 4 more: 11, 12, 13, 14.
quiz.mistake: Counts each bundle as 1, or writes 2 and 4 side by side

quiz.q: How do we show 7 with tally marks?
quiz.explain: 1 bundle is 5. 5 and 2 more make 7. So 1 bundle and ||.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each bundle is 1, or adds one line too many

quiz.q: Aisha's bird tally shows 1 bundle and |. Then 3 more birds come. How many birds now?
quiz.explain: 1 bundle and | is 5 + 1 = 6. Then 3 more: 6 + 3 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the new birds, or counts the bundle as 1

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I make tally marks for 5?
teach.praise: Yes! Draw 4 lines, then the 5th line goes across. A bundle of 5!
teach.nudge: How many lines do I draw first? Where does the 5th line go?

learn.hook: A graph made of pictures! Let's read a pictograph.
points: A pictograph uses pictures to show data.
Here, each picture stands for 1 thing.
Count the pictures in each row.
The row with the most pictures shows the most. The row with the fewest shows the least.

example.q: Mango 🥭🥭🥭🥭 and Banana 🍌🍌. How many more mangoes than bananas?

learn.reallife: Charts on the classroom wall show birthdays in each month or how children come to school.

items.text: The row with the most pictures is liked the ___.

quiz.q: Pictograph (each picture = 1 child): Laddoo 🟡🟡🟡🟡🟡, Jalebi 🟠🟠🟠. How many children like laddoo?
quiz.explain: Count the pictures in the laddoo row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
quiz.mistake: Reads the jalebi row, or counts both rows

quiz.q: Each picture = 1 child. Laddoo 🟡🟡🟡🟡🟡, Jalebi 🟠🟠🟠. How many more children like laddoo than jalebi?
quiz.explain: Laddoo 5, Jalebi 3. 5 − 3 = 2 more.
quiz.mistake: Adds the rows instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Pets: Dog 🐶🐶🐶🐶, Cat 🐱🐱, Fish 🐟🐟🐟. Which pet do the most children have?
quiz.explain: The dog row has 4 pictures. That is the most.
quiz.mistake: Picks the row with the fewest pictures

quiz.q: Pets: Dog 🐶🐶🐶🐶, Cat 🐱🐱, Fish 🐟🐟🐟. How many pets in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one row, or counts the rows instead of the pictures

quiz.q: In a pictograph, each ⭐ means 1 child. The cricket row has 7 stars. How many children chose cricket?
quiz.explain: Each star is 1 child. 7 stars means 7 children.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the whole row stands for 1 child

quiz.q: Trip pictograph: Bus 🚌🚌🚌, Train 🚆🚆🚆🚆🚆🚆, Car 🚗🚗. Which is liked the least?
quiz.explain: The car row has only 2 pictures. That is the fewest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the row with the most pictures

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I read a pictograph?
teach.praise: Wow! Count the pictures in each row. The most pictures means liked the most!
teach.nudge: What do I count in each row? Which row shows the most?
